title: Lost in a Book
description: Lost in a book, the lost in a book effect, uses an open volume as a door: near-plane paper, a gutter as threshold, illustration or weather coming out of the page, a reader looking in or falling in. A person reading on a couch is not the recipe.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Childhood, grief, a story that eats the teller: hands and paper close to lens, a world on the other side of the binding. Type should be unreadable texture so letters do not garble.
One world spills. A library wide with no portal is just a library.
It is the wrong tool when nothing leaves the page, and the wrong tool if you wanted a castle without a book. Fairytale castle is the destination.
This is the hinge.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Close enough that the book occupies the near third, 24mm to 50mm, lock-off or a tiny push into the gutter. Key from the page (light or weather leaving the paper) plus a dim room lamp.
Keep type as texture. Prompt: Lost-in-a-book of [Subject], a reader falling into illustration, pages becoming rooms.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: A child or adult at the threshold of a story, grief that opens a page, a tale that eats the teller. Do not use it as a couch-reading still with a closed book.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The NeverEnding Story makes the book a threshold you can fall through. Inkheart treats reading as a door with consequences.
The still should have paper in the near plane and a world leaving the gutter.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: A person reading on a couch, or a castle with no page. The tell is no threshold.
Fix it: open book in the near plane, something leaving the gutter, reader looking in or falling in.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Lost in a Book in film?
A portal recipe: an open book in the near plane, pages becoming rooms, a reader at the hinge. The book is a door, not a prop.
Lost in a Book vs Object Portal
Object portal is any object as a door. Lost in a book specifies paper, gutter, illustration spilling. If the door is a wardrobe or a screen, you wanted the generic cousin.
When should I use Lost in a Book?
Childhood, grief, a story that eats the teller. Skip library wides with no portal.
How do I prompt Lost in a Book for AI image or video?
Open book in foreground, then: Lost-in-a-book of [Subject], a reader falling into illustration, pages becoming rooms. Keep type unreadable. Show the hinge.
